items.followUp: Name two parts of an email message and state what each contains.

rubric.why: Identifies the message header and one of its details.
rubric.description: Names the header and a header detail such as sender, recipient, or subject.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the header and a detail it contains.

rubric.why: Identifies the body as the part carrying the message itself.
rubric.description: States that the body contains the main message content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the body and its content.

modelAnswer: An electronic message has a header and a body.
The header contains details such as the sender, recipient, and subject; the body contains the main message.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the HTML tag <h1>?

rubric.description:
Identifies

The

items.followUp: State one function of the Data Link Layer.

rubric.why: Identifies the layer's role in carrying data over the physical connection.
rubric.description: States that the Physical Layer transmits raw bits through a physical medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning transmission of bits over the medium.

rubric.why: Shows understanding that the layer represents bits as physical signals.
rubric.description: States that it converts or encodes bits into signals suitable for transmission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning conversion or encoding of bits into signals.

modelAnswer: The Physical Layer transmits raw bits from one device to another through the physical communication medium.
It represents the bits as signals and specifies physical transmission characteristics such as cables, connectors, and signalling.

items.followUp: What does HTTP stand for, and what is it used for?

rubric.why: Gives the correct expansion of FTP.
rubric.description: Expands FTP as File Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

rubric.why: States FTP's main purpose.
rubric.description: Explains that FTP is used to transfer files between computers over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing file transfer between computers.

modelAnswer: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.
It is used to transfer files between computers over a network, such as the Internet.

items.followUp: How can a shared network server help users store and access files?

rubric.why: Identifies shared network storage as the way capacity is increased.
rubric.description: States that a network can provide shared storage on a server or storage device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning shared server or network storage.

rubric.why: Explains the benefit to users and their computers.
rubric.description: Explains that users can store and access files on the shared storage instead of relying only on their own computer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining shared storage and access.

modelAnswer: A network can connect computers to a shared server or storage device with extra storage capacity.
Users can save files there and access them through the network, so they are not limited to the storage space on their own computers.

items.followUp: Explain how inputs and outputs are identified when defining a problem.

rubric.why: Shows that the problem must first be understood.
rubric.description: States that the problem situation and requirements are examined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the problem must be understood or analysed.

rubric.why: Identifies the data supplied to solve the problem.
rubric.description: Explains that inputs are the data or information provided.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining or identifying inputs.

rubric.why: Identifies the required result of the solution.
rubric.description: Explains that outputs are the results the solution must produce.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining or identifying outputs.

rubric.why: Includes important limits or conditions in the problem definition.
rubric.description: States that constraints, conditions, or the goal are specified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying constraints, conditions, or the goal.

modelAnswer: Defining a problem means clearly understanding and describing what needs to be solved.
Examine the problem and identify the information or data that will be provided as input.
Specify the result that the solution must produce as output.
State the goal and any constraints or conditions that the solution must satisfy.

items.followUp: Name the components of a data communication system and briefly describe any two.

rubric.why: Identifies the two communicating endpoints.
rubric.description: Names the sender and receiver and indicates their roles in communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sender and receiver as the communicating devices or parties.

rubric.why: Identifies the information being communicated.
rubric.description: Names the message as the data or information sent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the message.

rubric.why: Identifies the path used to carry the message.
rubric.description: Names the transmission medium or channel through which data travels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the medium or channel.

rubric.why: Identifies the rules that enable devices to communicate.
rubric.description: Names protocols and explains that they are communication rules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying protocols as the rules of communication.

modelAnswer: The basic components of data communication are sender, receiver, message, transmission medium, and protocol.
The sender sends the data, and the receiver gets it.
The message is the information being communicated, such as text, numbers, images, or sound.
The transmission medium carries the data between devices, while protocols are the rules followed for communication.

items.followUp: Explain phishing and identity theft as types of cybercrime.

rubric.why: Gives a valid type of cybercrime and explains its defining action.
rubric.description: Explains hacking as gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid explanation of hacking or unauthorised access.

rubric.why: Describes deception used to steal sensitive information.
rubric.description: Explains phishing as using fake messages or websites to trick people into revealing private information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of phishing.

rubric.why: Describes misuse of another person's identity or information.
rubric.description: Explains identity theft as stealing personal details to impersonate or defraud someone.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of identity theft.

rubric.why: Recognises another distinct form of cybercrime.
rubric.description: Names and briefly explains another type, such as cyberstalking, cyberbullying, malware distribution, or software piracy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and describing one additional valid type of cybercrime.

modelAnswer: Cybercrime is illegal activity carried out using computers or the Internet.
Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer, account, or network.
Phishing uses fake emails or websites to trick people into revealing passwords or other personal information.
Identity theft is stealing someone's personal details to impersonate or defraud that person.
Other forms include cyberstalking or cyberbullying, which use digital communication to harass or threaten people.
